changelog: feat: the chart editor now lives in the beta console. Customise charts used to send you to localhost:8000; it opens in place, and reads and writes the SAME file the production editor does — edit_charts/settings.json, shape {font, colors, sampleAliases, sampleOrder} — so a palette set in either console opens in the other and the R re-plot picks it up either way. Inventing a second settings file would have been far easier to write and would have split every job's styling in two depending on which console last touched it. It draws the taxonomy table as a stacked bar: rank picker across whatever taxonomy_*.csv the run produced, relative-abundance or read-count mode, per-taxon colour pickers, sample rename and reorder, title and font sizes, grid toggle, PNG export, and a table view. The SVG is hand-built because this page has no bundler and a lab machine has no network, which turned out to suit the house chart rules exactly: a 2px surface gap between stacked fills, 4px rounded ends on the outermost segments only, recessive axes, text in text tokens rather than series colour, a tooltip on every segment, and a legend always present. Three things it deliberately refuses to fudge. Taxa past the eighth fold into one grey 'Other' rather than being handed a ninth generated hue nobody can separate from the first eight — the palette is the validated categorical set (adjacent-pair CVD dE 9.1 light / 8.4 dark) and ends at eight. Unassigned reads never take a colour slot however numerous they are, and NA is routinely the largest 'genus' in a 16S table. And the orientation it read the CSV in is printed above the chart, because a silently transposed chart looks perfectly plausible and is completely wrong. Asking for more than eight taxa is allowed and says plainly that the colours stop being reliably distinguishable past that. Dark mode has its own series steps, not a flip of the light ones.
